Yihong Zhao赵一红

I am a master's student in Transportation Planning and Management at Beijing Jiaotong University. My work focuses on traffic-oriented GeoAI, spatiotemporal modeling, and urban road safety.

I use multi-source data and interpretable models to study how crash risk varies across places and to support more targeted safety decisions.

Research Interests

My research examines spatial heterogeneity and long-tailed risk in traffic safety. I combine GeoAI, spatially weighted models, Tweedie-LightGBM, and SHAP to study the effects of the built environment, traffic exposure, and electric-mobility infrastructure on crash risk.

Research & Projects

  1. 2026–present

    Weekly crash-risk forecasting for electric vehicles

    Master's thesis. I use rolling Tweedie-LightGBM models, neighboring-area risk history, and local explanations to identify high-risk areas under sparse, long-tailed crash distributions.

  2. 2026–present

    Knowledge-driven agent for urban traffic-risk analysis

    I combine street-level crash data, spatial risk predictions, local SHAP explanations, and a knowledge base to support natural-language queries, area comparisons, risk screening, and interpretable reports.

  3. 2025–2026

    Multi-scale GeoAI modeling of electric-vehicle fatal-crash risk

    I developed a multi-scale adaptive-bandwidth geographically weighted random forest (MSAB-GWRF) and spatially weighted SHAP framework to examine nonlinear and place-specific risk mechanisms. The work appeared in Accident Analysis & Prevention.
